## Code Review

This pull request streamlines the documentation for email inbox management and Meta Ads retargeting setup, replacing verbose step-by-step guides with concise tables and summarized operations. Review feedback highlights documentation inconsistencies in the email-inbox.md operations table, specifically where command arguments for triage and organization do not align with the provided helper script examples. Additionally, a suggestion was made to update a naming convention example in the retargeting guide to better reflect the recommended engagement options.

<details>
<summary>I am having trouble creating individual review comments. Click here to see my feedback.</summary>

### .agents/scripts/commands/email-inbox.md (18)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

There's an inconsistency in the `triage` command's documentation. The `Command` column shows `triage [--limit N]`, suggesting a user-configurable limit. However, the `Helper call` column has a hardcoded limit: `email-triage-helper.sh run --limit 50`. This could be misleading for an agent trying to use a custom limit. To ensure clarity, the helper call should reflect the variable limit, for example: `email-triage-helper.sh run --limit <N>`. Per repository guidelines, documentation for key helper scripts and commands must be accurate to support frequent use.

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. For clarity in documentation, restore key helper scripts and commands to domain index entries if they are frequently used, even if detailed documentation exists elsewhere.
</details>

### .agents/scripts/commands/email-inbox.md (24)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Similar to the `triage` command, there's an inconsistency with the `organize` command. The `Command` column `organize [--apply]` suggests an option to apply changes, but the `Helper call` column shows `email-mailbox-helper.sh organize --dry-run`, which would only preview them. If `--apply` is supported, the helper call should reflect that. Accurate documentation of helper commands is essential for agent reliability and clarity in domain index entries.

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. For clarity in documentation, restore key helper scripts and commands to domain index entries if they are frequently used, even if detailed documentation exists elsewhere.
</details>

### .agents/tools/marketing/meta-ads/audiences/retargeting-setup.md (170)

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The naming convention example `RT_Engage_PageLikes_60d` seems inconsistent with the engagement types described in the document. The 'Page and Instagram Engagement' section recommends using 'Engaged with any post or ad' but doesn't mention 'Page Likes' as an option. To avoid confusion, it would be better to use an example that directly corresponds to the options provided.

```suggestion
RT_Engage_PostAd_60d
```

</details>

## Code Review

This pull request refactors and condenses documentation for email inbox management and Meta Ads targeting strategies, primarily by converting descriptive sections into tables and removing detailed examples. Feedback indicates that the simplification was overly aggressive, resulting in the loss of critical information such as command usage examples, specific interest layering details, and actionable guidance for interpreting audience test results. It is recommended to restore these detailed reference elements to maintain the utility of the documentation while keeping the core structure concise.

## Code Review

This pull request refactors the `cmd_create` function in `github-release-helper.sh` by decomposing it into three sub-functions—`_parse_create_args`, `_resolve_create_inputs`, and `_execute_release_create`—and introduces module-scoped variables for state management. The review feedback suggests moving the initialization of these variables from the parsing function to the `cmd_create` orchestrator to avoid side effects and ensure the command's state is reset predictably.
